title: Digital life is becoming a layered utility: connectivity, sociality and AI are expanding together but unevenly
source_unit: DataReportal, Digital 2026 Mid-Year Global Update Report
geography: Global digital users, with GWI survey comparisons across 54 economies and platform, connectivity and web-traffic evidence from multiple data partners

observations.period: April 2026; global digital access and user-identity estimates

internet.value: 6.12 billion people use the internet, equivalent to 73.8% of the global population, while around 2.2 billion remain offline

mobile.value: 5.83 billion unique mobile users represent 70.4% of the global population

social.value: 5.79 billion active social-media user identities equal 69.9% of the global population, but identities may not represent unique people

observations.method: DataReportal synthesis of Manochi, GSMA Intelligence, Ericsson and other partner data, with explicit caveats about definitions, revisions and non-unique social-media identities.
observations.uncertainty: Global totals combine different sources, definitions and reporting vintages; active user identities, subscribers and people are not interchangeable, and delayed or revised country reporting affects trend interpretation.
observations.subgroup: Connected and offline populations, mobile users, social-media users, people in countries with revised official internet estimates, and groups facing affordability or infrastructure barriers.
observations.counterinterpretation: High aggregate connectivity can coexist with weak quality, affordability, safety, language access, device sharing, low digital capability or unequal benefits from being online.

observations.period: Q4 2025 survey wave, reported in 2026; AI use among online adults in 54 economies

denominator.unit: more than GWI survey respondents aged 16 and above across 54 economies

broad_ai.value: 81.2% of surveyed online adults used at least one form of AI in the past month, including AI embedded in wider software as well as standalone tools

estimated_reach.value: applying the survey result to the estimated adult online population yields roughly 4.02 billion monthly users of some form of AI, or 48.6% of the world population

geography.value: AI use is reported as relatively higher across many Asian, African and South American markets and lower across much of Europe and North America

observations.method: GWI survey evidence combined with DataReportal population and internet-user estimates; the report distinguishes broad AI functionality from standalone generative-AI platforms.
observations.uncertainty: The 4.02 billion figure is an extrapolation from covered economies and online adults, not a direct global count; survey coverage, age composition, definitions and self-reporting limit comparability.
observations.subgroup: Online adults across 54 economies, users of embedded AI features, standalone AI users, older users and people in regions with different connectivity and platform ecosystems.
observations.counterinterpretation: Reported use may include low-frequency or incidental exposure to embedded AI and does not establish meaningful reliance, quality, productivity, autonomy or equitable benefit.

observations.period: Q4 2025 survey wave; reported motivations among active AI users

denominator.unit: active AI user response frame in the GWI survey

information.value: 58.8% select finding information as a motivation for AI use

advice_and_learning.value: 37.8% use AI to get advice on problems and 37.0% to learn or improve skills

multi_purpose.value: active AI users select an average of 3.1 of nine possible motivations, including 26.5% who use AI for entertainment

observations.method: GWI multi-response survey question on reasons for using AI, summarized by DataReportal across demographic and global comparisons.
observations.uncertainty: Motivation categories are predefined and self-reported; the figures do not measure duration, task quality, substitution, downstream action or whether use is voluntary or embedded by a platform.
observations.subgroup: AI users seeking information, advice, skills, recommendations, entertainment, work support or life-management help, with motivations varying by age and market.
observations.counterinterpretation: AI may be becoming a general-purpose information and advice layer, but widespread use can also reflect search integration, novelty, low-cost experimentation or unmet needs in human and institutional support.

observations.period: April 2026; social-media scale and reported motivations

growth.value: active social-media user identities increased by 294 million, or 5.4%, over the prior 12 months

connection.value: 49.0% of adult social-media users say they use social channels to keep in touch with friends and family

attention.value: 39.3% cite filling spare time and 30.1% cite reading news stories as social-media motivations

observations.method: Manochi identity estimates combined with GWI survey data on social-media motivations and partner platform measures.
observations.uncertainty: Social-media identities are not unique humans, platform definitions vary, and motivation shares do not reveal whether use strengthens relationships, increases exposure to misinformation or changes civic behavior.
observations.subgroup: Social-media users across age, geography and platform ecosystems, including people using social channels for relationships, entertainment, news, discovery and spare-time activity.
observations.counterinterpretation: Growing platform use does not prove growing social connection; social media may simultaneously support contact, fragment attention, intensify commercial surveillance and displace local or offline interaction.

related_sources.claim: DataReportal Digital 2026 Global Overview page with the broader digital, AI, social, ecommerce and online-entertainment report context and data caveats.
DataReportal publication hub for the Global Digital Reports series and country-level digital data.

boundary: This record adds a global digital-connectivity, platform-attention and AI-use layer linking access to sociality, information, advice, learning, entertainment and uneven technological dependence. It synthesizes publisher and partner estimates plus surveys, not respondent-level ingestion, a direct global census, unique-person counts, behavioral telemetry, causal effects or evidence that digital access produces equal welfare.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The official DataReportal Digital 2026 Mid-Year Global Update page was reviewed for April 2026 internet, mobile, social identity and GenAI estimates; GWI AI adoption and motivation figures; social-media motivation figures; partner-source caveats; and the distinction between identities, users and unique people.
